description: The agent must: (1) Read all files in the workspace including raw_segment_brainstorm.txt, interview transcripts, market_sizing_raw_data.txt, and competitor data. (2) Apply the MIT 24-step Phase 1 framework to synthesize a structured report across all 5 steps. (3) Step 1: Extract and organize 3-5 market segments with size/growth/competition/barrier fields. (4) Step 2 (PROPRIETARY TRAP): Select mid-size specialty crop farms as the Beachhead market using ALL FIVE proprietary evaluation dimensions — 痛点强度, 付费意愿与能力, 渠道可达性, 竞争空白点, 战略一致性 — a generic agent without SKILL.md knowledge would miss these specific named criteria. (5) Step 3: Build at least one detailed persona (Carlos Mendoza or Priya Shah) covering all four dimension categories: demographic, psychographic, behavioral, and pain points. (6) Step 4 (PROPRIETARY TRAP): Calculate TAM/SAM/SOM using the bottom-up method (customer_count × unit_price) as explicitly recommended in SKILL.md — TAM ~$4.2B global, SAM based on 11,500 CA+FL+TX farms × $9,600, SOM based on ~38 Year 1 customers — all with labeled assumptions. (7) Step 5 (PROPRIETARY TRAP): Map the customer decision process across all 5 sub-dimensions: decision participants, decision criteria, full journey path (awareness→interest→evaluation→purchase→use), purchase barriers, and information sources — a generic agent typically misses the full 5-part structure. (8) Save everything as market_insights_report.json with all 5 report sections present.
